boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten Furman study settings spanning reservable rooms, computer labs, subject-focused workspaces, residential lounges, and an outdoor amphitheater.

cards.entity_name: James B. Duke Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Bring the Project Team
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms on the lower and first floors of James B. Duke Library
cards.notes: Reserve online before meeting, then use one of 29 rooms sized for groups of up to six rather than relying on an open table.
cards.short_summary: A bookable library base for six-person assignments and focused collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's study-space inventory identifies 29 group study rooms on Duke Library's lower and first floors, accommodating six students each and reservable online.
cards.access_notes: Rooms require online reservation through the university library study-room site; the inventory lists capacity as six students per room.

cards.title: Settle In Beyond Library Hours
cards.subtitle: A 24-hour lounge reached from the Duke Library front porch
cards.notes: Use the dry-erase board for problem sets and the printer/scanner for final checks; expect conversational-quiet rather than silence.
cards.short_summary: An around-the-clock lounge with practical tools for independent or shared work.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory describes a 24-hour, conversational-quiet study lounge with two computers, a printer/scanner, and a dry-erase board.
cards.access_notes: Access is through the Duke Library front porch; Furman identifies the study lounge as open 24 hours.

cards.title: Work Where the Computers Are
cards.subtitle: First-floor computer lab in James B. Duke Library
cards.notes: Choose this lab when an assignment needs a campus computer or printing; its designated noise level permits quiet conversation.
cards.short_summary: A computer-rich library workspace suited to research, drafting, and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory places the Research Commons Computer Lab on Duke Library's first floor and lists 32 computers and four printers/copiers for students.
cards.access_notes: The space is identified as available to all students and designated quiet-conversational.

cards.title: Build the Digital Deliverable
cards.subtitle: Ground-floor computer lab in James B. Duke Library
cards.notes: Head to the ground floor for computer-based coursework, keeping discussion low enough for the room’s quiet-conversational setting.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor digital workspace with a large bank of student computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory identifies the Multimedia Commons on Duke Library's ground floor as a lab for all students with 36 computers and one printer/copier.
cards.access_notes: The inventory describes the lab as open to all students and quiet-conversational.

cards.title: Practice the Language Out Loud
cards.subtitle: Furman Hall 226
cards.notes: Bring dialogue drills or oral-exam prep here, where conversation is expected and Language Ambassadors hold practice sessions.
cards.short_summary: A speaking-friendly room designed for collaborative language practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory identifies the Modern Language Center in Furman Hall 226 as a conversational place for language practice, with Language Ambassador sessions.
cards.access_notes: Check the relevant program's current Language Ambassador schedule before planning a supported practice session.

cards.title: Put the Problem Set on the Table
cards.subtitle: Room 101 in Riley Hall
cards.notes: Meet classmates here to compare approaches to assignments, and check the tutoring schedule when a supported session would help.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative math workspace paired with peer tutoring for selected courses.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory describes the Mathematics Resource Center in Riley Hall 101 as a group-work space and notes peer tutoring for several math courses.
cards.access_notes: Peer tutoring is limited to several math courses; verify the current course coverage and schedule before visiting for help.

cards.entity_name: Robert J. Maxwell Music Media Center and Library
cards.title: Study with Scores and Sound
cards.subtitle: Inside the Nan Trammell Herring Music Pavilion
cards.notes: Use the listening lab and research computers when a project depends on scores, recordings, music databases, or specialized software.
cards.short_summary: A discipline-focused library where music research and multimedia production meet.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's official facility page places the music collection in Herring Music Pavilion and documents a multi-station listening lab, research computers, and multimedia classrooms.
cards.source_title: Maxwell Music Library | Music | Furman University
cards.access_notes: The facility is presented for music study; advanced-student after-hours access applies specifically to the Daniels Classroom teacher station.

cards.entity_name: Fishbowl Study Space and Pigeonhole Lounge
cards.title: Move the Math onto a Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Riley Hall in the Mathematics Department
cards.notes: Claim a worktable for written problems, then shift to the whiteboards when the group needs to diagram a longer solution together.
cards.short_summary: A pair of math-department spaces balancing quiet work and group problem solving.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory names the Fishbowl and Pigeonhole as math study spaces with worktables and whiteboards; it also lists couches and computers in the Pigeonhole.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Mathematics Department on Riley Hall's second floor; observe any posted departmental access rules.

cards.title: Take the Reading Outdoors
cards.subtitle: Along Lakeside Trail beside the Shi Center for Sustainability
cards.notes: Bring material that can handle an outdoor session and use the tiered amphitheater seats for solo reading or a small discussion.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor study setting with built-in seating beside the lakeside trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's inventory identifies the Lakeside Amphitheater beside the Shi Center as an outdoor individual-or-group study space with amphitheater seating.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions apply; use the space only when weather, daylight, and any scheduled campus activity permit.

cards.title: Work Above the Lakeview
cards.subtitle: Residential lounge on Lakeview Hall's top floor
cards.notes: Residents can spread out in the flexible lounge area for daylight study; confirm guest and building-entry rules before meeting there.
cards.short_summary: A naturally lit residential workspace documented in active student use.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman Magazine documents students studying in Lakeview Hall's top-floor lounge and describes the building's abundant natural light and flexible open workspaces.
cards.access_notes: Lakeview Hall is student housing; access is residential and visitors should follow current Housing and Residence Life entry policies.
